3.speaker: Narrator
3.text: I signed the document altering the ownership of the key corporations with a flourish. Symon leaned back in his chair.

5.speaker: Symon Holl
5.text: “This is the path we are taking.”

19.speaker: Mikail Aven
19.text: “Symon, please tell me you are not fine with this.”

20.speaker: Mikail Aven
20.text: “Please tell me...that Mr. President...did not just sign this order.”

22.speaker: Lucian Galade
22.text: “And there is nothing you can do about it.”

24.speaker: Narrator
24.text: Mikail turned to me. His eyes were wide open with rage. He was clenching his fists so hard that his hands turned red from exertion.

27.speaker: Player
27.text: “What did you just call me? Say that again. I dare you."

31.speaker: Narrator
31.text: Two security officers immediately entered the room with hands on their guns.

32.speaker: Narrator
32.text: They looked at me expectantly, waiting for my orders.

33.speaker: Player
33.text: “A few years in Antel Rock Prison will teach him how to talk to a President. Take him away.”

37.speaker: Player
37.text: “It's all fine. Just a disagreement. Right, Mr. Aven?”

39.speaker: Player
39.text: “Please calm down, Mr. Aven. Otherwise I will have you removed.”

40.speaker: Player
40.text: “Go back to your master like the dog you are and tell Mr. Tusk you're through.”

42.speaker: Edith Agnoc
42.text: “I am very sorry for my colleague's behavior, Mr. President.”

43.speaker: Edith Agnoc
43.text: “I hope we can look past this.”

44.speaker: Edith Agnoc
44.text: “I'm sure Mikail is sorry too. Right?”

45.speaker: Mikail Aven
45.text: “I am sorry, Mr. President. I lost my cool.”

46.speaker: Player
46.text: “We all make mistakes. I forgive you.”

51.speaker: Mikail Aven
51.text: “Come, Edith. We must report the outcome of this meeting.”

53.speaker: Narrator
53.text: Mikail turned to Edith with a sour face. His eyes were shooting daggers.

55.speaker: Narrator
55.text: He packed up his bag and started making his way to the entrance.

56.speaker: Narrator
56.text: Lucian got up from his seat and intercepted him on his way out. He put his hand on Mikail's shoulder and spoke with a calm and soft voice.

59.speaker: Narrator
59.text: Mikail didn't respond. He simply left.

60.speaker: Edith Agnoc
60.text: “Mr. President. Please, he didn't mean it like that.”

61.speaker: Edith Agnoc
61.text: “We all make mistakes and I know what a kind and benevolent President you are.”

63.speaker: Narrator
63.text: The guards flanked Mikail and grabbed his arms from both sides.

68.speaker: Mikail Aven
68.text: “Get off of me, you lowlifes! Don't you know who I am?”

70.speaker: Narrator
70.text: He started struggling but the guards held him tightly.

71.speaker: Narrator
71.text: The door closed and his muffled protests gradually faded away.

73.speaker: Narrator
73.text: Edith made her way to Mikail and gestured for him to leave the room with her.

78.speaker: Narrator
78.text: He measured the guards with his eyes.

79.speaker: Mikail Aven
79.text: “I am very sorry about that, Mr. President.”

80.speaker: Narrator
80.text: Guards flanked Mikail and grabbed his arms from both sides.

83.speaker: Mikail Aven
83.text: “What did you just say to m--”

84.speaker: Mikail Aven
84.text: “Mr. Tusk will hear about this. You can rest assured.”

85.speaker: Mikail Aven
85.text: “Although I am very much against the nationalization of any company, I am glad you at least chose to leave Bergia Steel alone."

87.text: “Now we must look into implementing these changes.”

89.speaker: Mikail Aven
89.text: “Before you start that discussion, I'm afraid Edith and I will have to leave.”

90.speaker: Mikail Aven
90.text: “We need to report the outcome to our companies to make sure we can mitigate the impact.”

91.speaker: Edith Agnoc
91.text: “Thank you everyone. Have a nice day.”

92.speaker: Narrator
92.text: They gathered their belongings and left the room hurriedly.

93.speaker: Mikail Aven

166.text: “I want to thank you, Mr. President.”

167.speaker: Mikail Aven
167.text: “This decision will revitalize our economy. Eliminating recession completely is not so far off now.”

168.speaker: Edith Agnoc
168.text: “This will definitely show our trade partners that Sordland is moving in the right direction. Which in turn will increase trust... which means more income.”

172.speaker: Lucian Galade
172.text: “Yes, fully privatizing state corporations might give us the budget boost required to help us end the recession.”

173.speaker: Lucian Galade
173.text: “But we can only pave the way forward for Sordland if we are leading the country from the top.”

174.speaker: Lucian Galade
174.text: “Mr. President. Your decision will cost us the support of *every* *single* conservative in the Assembly.”

176.speaker: Player
176.text: “We can offset our losses in votes with our gains from this change.”

178.speaker: Lucian Galade
178.text: “Of course, that includes the leader of the conservative wing of our own party, Gloria Tory.”

179.speaker: Lucian Galade
179.text: “I also want to remind you that the majority of the Assembly is conservative. We have our work cut out for us.”

180.speaker: Lucian Galade
180.text: “You are being too optimistic. I'm afraid of the reality.”

183.speaker: Narrator
183.text: He frowned, bowed slightly and spoke with a soft voice.

184.speaker: Lucian Galade
184.text: “I will see what we can do, but this might be the hardest task you have ever given me.”

185.speaker: Player
185.text: “I have complete trust in your capabilities, Lucian.”

187.speaker: Player
187.text: “We have come this far. We can handle it.”

189.speaker: Lucian Galade
189.text: “If you will excuse me, I have to get to work immediately. There is much to be done.”

190.speaker: Narrator

212.text: “Partial privatization will still deal damage to our conservative voter base. But it is nothing we can't handle.”

213.speaker: Lucian Galade
213.text: “I believe this was the best outcome we could have hoped for.”

218.speaker: Lucian Galade
218.text: “But the gains we receive will offset the losses.”

222.speaker: Lucian Galade

223.speaker: Lucian Galade

224.speaker: Lucian Galade

225.speaker: Lucian Galade

226.speaker: Lucian Galade
